correctness.rationale: Let τ=cos(π/9), σ=cos(2π/9), θ0=7π/9. At θ=π the (cosθ,cos4θ,cos5θ) signs are (−1,1,−1), while at θ0 they are (−σ,−τ,τ). Thus for any globally nonnegative candidate, τT(π)+T(θ0)=1+τ−a(τ+σ)≥0, implying a≤(1+τ)/(τ+σ)=2 cos(π/18)/√3. The proposed a,b,c at r=cos(7π/9) satisfy 8r³−6r−1=0 and factor T(arccos x)=(x+1)(x−r)²R_r(x)/[(9/2)(8r²−6r−1)]. I independently reduced the identity modulo the cubic in exact symbolic arithmetic, verified the residual quadratic has positive leading coefficient and negative discriminant, and the denominator is positive for r∈(−1,−3/4). Thus T≥0 for every x∈[−1,1], not only on sampled θ. Both positive-weight contact points must vanish for equality; interior zero derivative forces a third independent linear equation and fixes b,c uniquely. Independent symbolic check gives 3a³−3a−1=0. Numerically sampled positivity is merely supplementary.

value.rationale: M(H) for a natural two-element sparse harmonic support is an explicitly posed invariant in classical Carathéodory–Fejér support problems. The exact cutoff includes a unique extremal polynomial and an algebraic dual certificate, useful as a benchmark for sparse positive trigonometric polynomials and potential two-frequency classifications. The calculation is not a known-table recomputation, a pure substitution of H={3,4}, or an arbitrary angle slice: the contact frequencies determine new algebraic constraints and positivity factorization.
residual_risks: It is one exact finite support, not a complete two-element H taxonomy.
